cards.a: Prove your meter on a known live source, test the circuit for absence of voltage, then prove the meter again.
cards.tip: The meter is checked twice; the circuit once.

cards.a: Approximately 4 to 6 milliamperes of ground-fault current.
cards.tip: “Four to six keeps hearts in ticks.”

cards.a: The Canadian workplace electrical safety standard covering safe work practices, arc flash and shock protection.
cards.tip: CEC = installation; Z462 = how you work on it.

cards.a: E = I × R. Voltage equals current times resistance.
cards.tip: Cover the unknown in the E-I-R triangle.

cards.a: Current is the same everywhere; source voltage divides across the loads.
Voltage is the same across every branch; current divides inversely with resistance.
Power lost as heat equals current squared times resistance — doubling current quadruples the heat.
cards.tip: Loose (resistive) joints burn because of I²R.

cards.a: Around any closed loop, the sum of voltage drops equals the source voltage.
cards.tip: What the source gives, the loop takes.

cards.a: The effective value of an AC quantity — equal in heating effect to the same DC value. Meters read RMS.
In an inductor (L), voltage E leads current I. In a capacitor (C), current I leads voltage E.
cards.tip: Say it out loud in the exam — everyone does.

cards.a: XL = 2πfL, in ohms. Rises with frequency and inductance.
cards.tip: L likes low frequency; XL grows as f grows.

cards.a: XC = 1 ÷ (2πfC), in ohms. Falls as frequency rises.
Total AC opposition: Z = √(R² + X²), in ohms.
True power divided by apparent power: PF = W ÷ VA = cos θ. Never greater than 1.
Three windings joined at a common neutral point. Line voltage = phase voltage × √3.
cards.tip: The letter Y has a centre — so does the connection.

cards.a: Three windings joined end-to-end in a closed triangle; no neutral. Line current = phase current × √3.
1.732 — the factor in every three-phase line calculation.
The percentage by which rotor speed falls below synchronous speed; typically 2–5% at full load.
cards.tip: No slip, no torque in an induction motor.

cards.a: Interchange any two line conductors.
EP ÷ ES = NP ÷ NS. Voltage follows turns; current follows the inverse.
cards.tip: Step voltage down, current steps up.

cards.a: Transformers are rated in kVA because winding heat depends on current regardless of power factor.
Never open a current transformer's secondary while the primary is energized — dangerous voltage develops.
cards.tip: Short it before you lift a meter.

cards.a: The maximum current a conductor can carry continuously under its conditions of use.
cards.tip: Insulation, ambient, grouping, termination — four checks.

cards.a: Grounding ties the system to earth; bonding ties metal parts together to carry fault current and trip the protection.
cards.tip: “Grounding goes to ground; bonding bonds the boxes.”

cards.a: #14 Cu → 15 A, #12 Cu → 20 A, #10 Cu → 30 A maximum overcurrent protection.
Limited to 80% of the overcurrent device rating unless the assembly is 100%-rated.
Three or more conductors may fill a maximum of 40% of the raceway cross-section.
Start–stop with a seal-in contact: provides low-voltage protection, so no automatic restart after an outage.
Normally closed, wired in series — any one opening stops the motor. Starts are normally open, in parallel.
